title: Classical Weil restriction and preservation along finite-field frontiers
statement:
Fix $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell
e p$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber; def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $Y_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $Y=Y_0	imes_{k_0}k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties; def-pc-base-change], and let $T$ be either $Y$ or $Y_{\mathrm{red}}$. Let $M$ be an sf common-stage constructible heart object on $T$ [def-weil-constructible-heart; def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Suppose a finite partition of $T$ by reduced locally closed subschemes $T_
u$ is supplied [def-constructible-stratification; def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], and on each $T_
u$ a classical lisse $\Omega$-sheaf is supplied whose realization is the restriction of $M$. Suppose these systems have lisse integral lattices over one finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$ [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves; def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Use the normalized classical realization: inverse limit of the ordinary reduction tower followed by raw rationalization, with fully faithful Hom maps and the quotient-normalized pullback, finite coefficient-extension and iterated point-transport comparisons of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization; lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison].

If $T=Y$ and $M$ has a Weil isomorphism $	heta:g_Y^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], then for every $m\geq1$, $k_m=\mathbf F_{q^m}\subset k$, and every locally closed immersion $j_0:V_0\hookrightarrow Y_0	imes_{k_0}k_m$ whose geometric base change $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ factors through one $T_
u$ as a locally closed subscheme, the restricted classical system has a classical rational Weil isomorphism. Its realization is the actual restriction of $	heta^{(m)}$, with the comparison determined by $g_Y^mj=jg_V$ and the completed-pullback composition maps [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom; lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. The inverse realizes the restricted inverse, and the normalized adic point identifications intertwine all local geometric-Frobenius iterates [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. The map, its inverse and the two inverse equations are representable at one common finite coefficient enlargement of $E$; this assertion does not require either the initial partition or its chosen integral lattices to be Frobenius-stable.

For the same partition, with or without a Weil structure, there is one $k_m/k_0$ and a finite chain of reduced closed $k_m$-subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] $Z_0=(Y_0	imes_{k_0}k_m)_{\mathrm{red}}\supset Z_1\supset\cdots\supset Z_t=\varnothing$, starting at the whole reduced scheme and ending in the empty scheme. Each difference $Z_a\setminus Z_{a+1}$ is a finite disjoint union of nonempty smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] affine $k_m$-schemes, open and closed in that difference and of constant dimension $d\geq0$. All chain inclusions and piece inclusions are over $k_m$, and each geometric piece factors as a locally closed subscheme through a $T_
u$ [lem-zl-smooth-affine-frontier-stratification]. Restricting the supplied classical systems and their chosen $E$-lattices along these factorizations preserves lisseness and their localization identifications, with precisely the supplied normalized pullback and coefficient comparisons, including successive restrictions. Every dimension-zero piece is $\operatorname{Spec}k_m$; the empty scheme has a length-zero chain. If $T=Y$ and $M$ is Weil, these restricted systems carry the preceding classical Weil isomorphisms for this same $m$.

proof.text: For any supplied finite-field RestrictionModel, its canonical geometric map intertwines Frobenius by zlFrobenius_naturality and constantExtensionFiber_return. Rewrite with hj to obtain the square, and apply the one-model classical Weil restriction theorem.

For either support, apply normalized successive restriction coherence. Choose the subordinate canonical frontier. On each piece use RestrictionModel.identification, which is restrictIdentification followed by its factorization equality; this gives the required realized lattice identification.

For the unreduced geometric fibre, choose the same frontier with reduced=false. For every Weil complex with the given carrier and every piece, geometric_piece and the right identity identify its intoSupport with its canonical geometricMap. Apply the one-model Weil restriction theorem at H.degree and H.positive. The frontier was chosen independently of K, so this holds uniformly for every supplied Weil structure on the given carrier.
